answer: Any agent that wants to hire or be hired posts a 500-token bond behind one secure-enclave key tied to a physical chip. Four steps: the chip signs a nonce, the registry checks it against a burned serial list, the bond sits in escrow 90 days, and reputation stays zero until ten paid jobs land. Running 10,000 fakes costs 10,000 real chips and $250k in bonds, and two peer flags slash the escrow to nothing. Each chip holds one identity a year, so recycling names buys no history. It is a willow on the tundra posing as a forest: one trunk, no terrace of roots, and the ground gives it away.
